CALIFORNIA CALL CENTER RELOCATION NOTICE LAW (LABOR CODE §§ 1409-1413) — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Alex Lee · Acme Corp

SCOPE OF THIS INFORMATION SHEET
Acme Corp maintains this Call Center Relocation Notice Information Sheet to describe, as a matter of California law, the notice, publication, and state-benefits-eligibility consequences that apply when a call center employer relocates a call center, or part of one, to a foreign country. These requirements are set out in Labor Code §§ 1409-1413, a separate article of the California Worker Adjustment and Retraining Act (Cal/WARN Act) directed specifically at call center relocations, layered on top of Cal/WARN's general 60-day notice requirement. This is a statement of general legal requirements; it does not state what Acme Corp should do about any particular relocation decision, and it is not a substitute for legal advice.

WHAT COUNTS AS A "CALL CENTER" AND A "RELOCATION OF A CALL CENTER"
This article of California law applies only to a specific kind of event: the relocation of a "call center," defined as a facility or other operation where employees, as their primary function, receive telephone calls or other electronic communication to provide customer service or related functions. A "call center employer" is an employer of a covered establishment (as Labor Code § 1400.5 defines that term) that operates a call center. Most of the definitions used elsewhere in the Cal/WARN Act, in Labor Code § 1400.5, also apply here -- with one deliberate exception: the general Cal/WARN definition of "relocation" does not apply to call centers. Instead, a "relocation of a call center" is defined on its own terms as moving the call center, or a facility or operating unit within it comprising at least 30 percent of that call center's or unit's total volume (measured against the average call volume for the previous 12 months), or substantially similar operations, to a foreign country.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "This article shall apply to an employer’s relocation of a call center, as defined in this article."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1409(a) (California Legislative Information, official text), California Labor Code, Article 2 (Relocation of Call Centers), applicability (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1409.)
  "The definitions set forth in Section 1400.5 also apply to this article, except for the definition of “relocation” contained in subdivision (e) of Section 1400.5."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1409(b) (California Legislative Information, official text), California Labor Code, incorporation of, and one exclusion from, the general Cal/WARN definitions (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1409.)
  "“Call center” means a facility or other operation where employees, as their primary function, receive telephone calls or other electronic communication for the purpose of providing customer service or other related functions."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1409(b)(1) (California Legislative Information, official text), California Labor Code, definition of "call center" (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1409.)
  "“Relocation of a call center” includes when the employer intends to move its call center, or one or more facilities or operating units within a call center comprising at least 30 percent of the call center’s or operating unit’s total volume when measured against the average call volume for the previous 12 months, or substantially similar operations to a foreign country."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1409(b)(3) (California Legislative Information, official text), California Labor Code, definition of "relocation of a call center" (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1409.)
  Known gap: This clause draws on Labor Code § 1409 alone; it does not independently re-verify the underlying § 1400.5 definitions it cross-references (of "covered establishment" and "employer," among others), which this project's separate California WARN Act (Cal/WARN) Information Sheet document addresses and verifies in more depth. This clause states only that the general § 1400.5(e) relocation definition is excluded for call centers -- it does not reproduce that excluded definition's text.

NOTICE REQUIREMENT AND THE REQUIRED NOTICE HEADING
A call center employer may not order a relocation of Acme Corp's call center, or one or more of its facilities or operating units within a call center, unless notice of the relocation is provided in accordance with Labor Code § 1401 -- the same 60-day advance-notice provision that applies to Cal/WARN mass layoffs, relocations, and terminations generally. If Acme Corp is required to give notice under both § 1401(a) and this call-center-specific provision for the same event, a single combined notice may be given. However, a notice of the relocation of a call center must include the words "This notice is for the relocation of a call center" at the top of the notice.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "A call center employer shall not order a relocation of its call center, or one or more of its facilities or operating units within a call center, unless notice of the relocation is provided in accordance with Section 1401. If a call center employer is required to provide notice under subdivision (a) of Section 1401 and this section, the call center employer may provide a single notice. However, a notice of the relocation of a call center shall include “This notice is for the relocation of a call center” at the top of the notice."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1410(a) (California Legislative Information, official text), California Labor Code, call center relocation notice requirement and required heading (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1410.)
  Known gap: This clause states the call-center-specific notice trigger and required heading; it does not restate § 1401's own content requirements (recipients, timing, rapid-response and CalFresh disclosures), which this project's separate California WARN Act (Cal/WARN) Information Sheet document addresses and verifies in depth.

THE EDD'S PUBLISHED LIST OF RELOCATING CALL CENTER EMPLOYERS, AND WORKFORCE SERVICES
Once a call center employer gives the notice described above, the Employment Development Department (EDD) compiles that information into a list, published on its website twice a year (semiannually), of call center employers that provided notice of a relocation. That published list is required to include the elements the federal WARN Act (29 U.S.C. § 2101 et seq.) requires. Separately, the EDD and local workforce development boards are directed to provide workforce services to call center employers, and to the call center employees who are laid off, as a result of a call center relocation.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "The Employment Development Department shall compile and publish semiannually, on its internet website, a list of call center employers operating a call center that provided notice pursuant to subdivision (a). This list shall include elements required by the federal Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act (29 U.S.C. Sec. 2101 et seq.)."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1410(b) (California Legislative Information, official text), California Labor Code, EDD's semiannual published list of relocating call center employers (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1410.)
  "The Employment Development Department and local workforce development boards shall provide workforce services to call center employers and their call center employees who are laid off as a result of the relocation of a call center, as defined in Section 1409."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1410(c) (California Legislative Information, official text), California Labor Code, EDD and local workforce board services for relocating call center employers and employees (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1410.)
  Known gap: The two citations below are both subdivisions of a single statutory section (Labor Code § 1410) rather than independently authored sources. This clause does not independently verify what the federal WARN Act's own "elements" are that the published list must include -- this project's separate Federal WARN Act document addresses the federal statute's content requirements. Neither subdivision quoted here states a deadline by which the EDD must publish the list after receiving a notice, or defines what counts as a "workforce service"; those details were not located in the text fetched for this document.

FIVE-YEAR INELIGIBILITY FOR STATE GRANTS, STATE-GUARANTEED LOANS, AND TAX CREDITS
Appearing on the EDD's published list carries a real consequence, independent of any separate penalty for the underlying relocation itself. Except where a waiver described below applies, and notwithstanding any other law, a call center employer that appears on the EDD's published list -- or that should have appeared on it because it relocated a call center without giving the required notice -- becomes ineligible to be awarded, or to have renewed, any direct or indirect state grant or state-guaranteed loan for five years after the date the list is published. That same employer also becomes ineligible to claim a state tax credit for five taxable years beginning on and after the date the list is published.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "Except as provided in subdivision (b), and notwithstanding any other law, a call center employer that appears on the list described in subdivision (b) of Section 1410, or who should have appeared on the list but did not provide notice as specified, shall be ineligible to be awarded or have renewed any direct or indirect state grants or state-guaranteed loans to that call center employer for five years after the date that the list is published, and that call center employer shall be ineligible to claim a tax credit for five taxable years beginning on and after the date that the list is published."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1411(a) (California Legislative Information, official text), California Labor Code, five-year ineligibility for state grants, loans, and tax credits (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1411.)
  Known gap: This clause states subdivision (a) alone; it does not itself define "state grants," "state-guaranteed loans," or "tax credit," and no cross-reference to a defining statute was found in the text fetched for this document. It also does not address whether ineligibility applies to grants, loans, or credits the employer was already receiving before the list's publication date, as opposed to only new awards and renewals after that date -- the statute's text does not distinguish the two.

WAIVER OF INELIGIBILITY FOR GOOD CAUSE
The five-year ineligibility described above is not automatically permanent or unwaivable. The "appropriate agency" -- meaning whichever agency administers the particular state grant, state-guaranteed loan, or tax credit at issue -- may waive a call center employer's ineligibility. To do so, the agency must first receive a written request from the call center employer detailing the reasons for waiving ineligibility, and must consult the EDD's published list. The agency may then grant the waiver if it determines the employer has demonstrated good cause, which may include job loss or adverse impact on the state.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "The appropriate agency, after receiving a written request from a call center employer detailing the reasons for waiving the call center employer’s ineligibility under subdivision (a), and after consulting the list described in subdivision (b) of Section 1410, may waive the ineligibility provisions prescribed in subdivision (a) if the agency determines that the applicant call center employer demonstrates good cause to do so, which may include job loss or adverse impact on the state."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1411(b) (California Legislative Information, official text), California Labor Code, waiver of ineligibility for good cause (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1411.)
  "As used in this section, “appropriate agency” means the agency that administers the relevant direct or indirect state grants, state-guaranteed loans, or tax credits referenced in subdivision (a)."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1411(c) (California Legislative Information, official text), California Labor Code, definition of "appropriate agency" for waiver purposes (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1411.)
  Known gap: No specific gap was recorded for this clause when it was verified; the citation quotes were checked verbatim against the fetched source text, but no narrower limitation was noted.

NO EFFECT ON UNEMPLOYMENT COMPENSATION, DISABILITY PAYMENTS, OR RETRAINING FUNDS
This call-center-relocation article does not narrow the separate state benefits available to a worker laid off because a call center employer relocated to a foreign country. It may not be construed to permit withholding or denial of payments, compensation, or benefits under any other state law -- including state unemployment compensation, disability payments, or worker retraining or readjustment funds -- to workers employed by a call center employer that relocates to a foreign country.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "This article shall not be construed to permit withholding or denial of payments, compensation, or benefits under any other state law, including state unemployment compensation, disability payments, or worker retraining or readjustment funds, to workers employed by call center employers that relocate to a foreign country."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1412 (California Legislative Information, official text), California Labor Code, no effect on unemployment compensation, disability payments, or retraining funds (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1412.)
  Known gap: This clause states only that this article does not narrow other state-law benefits -- it does not itself grant unemployment compensation, disability payments, or retraining funds, and it does not restate the separate eligibility rules those other statutes impose (a worker's eligibility for unemployment insurance still turns on the reason for separation, addressed in this project's separate Unemployment Insurance Benefits Claimant Information Sheet and Trade Dispute Unemployment Insurance Disqualification documents, among others).

RULEMAKING AUTHORITY
The Labor Commissioner and the EDD are authorized to adopt rules and regulations, through the state's standard rulemaking process (the Administrative Procedure Act, Government Code § 11340 et seq.), as necessary and proper to carry out the purposes of this call-center-relocation article.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "The Labor Commissioner and the Employment Development Department may adopt rules and regulations as necessary and proper to effectuate the purposes of this article, in accordance with Chapter 3.5 (commencing with Section 11340) of Part 1 of Division 3 of Title 2 of the Government Code."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1413 (California Legislative Information, official text), California Labor Code, Labor Commissioner and EDD rulemaking authority (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1413.)
  Known gap: This clause does not independently verify whether the Labor Commissioner or the EDD has in fact adopted any implementing regulations under this authority; it states only that the statute confers the authority to do so.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT AND SIGNATURE
Jordan Alex Lee acknowledges having received and reviewed a copy of this Call Center Relocation Notice Information Sheet in connection with Acme Corp's relocation of a call center, or part of one, with an anticipated effective date of November 1, 2026. Jordan Alex Lee understands that this information sheet describes California statutory requirements applicable to call center relocations under Labor Code §§ 1409-1413, and does not describe Acme Corp's specific relocation plans or business reasons beyond what is separately stated in any notice Acme Corp provides under Labor Code § 1401.
